correctness.rationale: The exact polynomial payoffs at w=1 make z*=(2/3,2) an interior equilibrium. J=[[1/6,1/6],[-3epsilon/2,-3epsilon/8]] has trace (4-9epsilon)/24<0 and determinant 3epsilon/16>0 for epsilon>4/9; a nonresonant analytic period-map IFT gives the unique nearby attracting interior T=2pi/omega response at any fixed omega>0. The first harmonic h=(i omega I-J)^(-1)g and quadratic averaged Taylor forcing -J^(-1)Q produce mean second coefficient -256omega²(3epsilon+4)/(9[(9epsilon-48omega²)²+(18epsilon-8)²omega²]); half-period symmetry kills odd orders, and optimizing over omega² gives omega*=sqrt(3epsilon)/4. Independently differentiated the payoff equations and computed exact Jacobian, forcing and quadratic response at epsilon=1, omega=sqrt(3)/4: -448/225. The local, fixed-parameter and infinitesimal limits are explicit.
residual_risks: No global attraction, finite-amplitude sign, or uniformity near the Hopf boundary epsilon=4/9 or omega=0 follows.

value.rationale: The same public-goods model is used to investigate how periodic environments change coexistence. An exact negative sign for ordinary mean cooperation at every positive forcing frequency, plus a unique sharp resonance omega*=sqrt(3epsilon)/4, supplies a motivated quantitative observable that is not determined by the prior weighted balance. It distinguishes slow/fast weak forcing from resonant suppression over a continuous range of feedback speeds.
residual_risks: Only the small-amplitude locally attracting branch is proved, not a finite-amplitude global effect.
